title: Can we always tell which angle is greater by looking?
description: Two angles with very different openings are quick to compare by eye. Two angles with nearly the same opening look alike, so one is laid over the other to be sure. Keeko's doubt is that we can always tell by looking.
teaching_notes: One idea: angles with nearly the same opening cannot be compared by eye, so we lay one over the other or measure them. Watch for students who trust their eyes for every pair of angles.

source: Is it always easy to compare two angles?
video_script.why: The child sees that angles of nearly the same size cannot be compared by looking alone.
video_script.substitution: the book's question on whether it is always simple to compare two angles
video_script.anchor: two pairs of angles, one pair far apart in size and one pair almost the same size
video_script.wrong_answer: you can always tell by looking
video_script.wrong_move: trusts the eye for angles that are almost the same size
video_script.payoff_line: No, it is not always simple to compare two angles

final_answer.spoken: no, it is not always simple to compare two angles

hold_back: No, it is not always simple
maths_rules: angles with very different openings can be compared at a glance
angles with nearly the same opening look alike, so the eye cannot say which is greater
to be sure, lay one angle over the other with the vertices together, or measure both
slip: looking is not a safe way to compare angles that are nearly equal
video_script.design: One idea: close angles need superimposition or measuring. Two pairs of angles stay on the board, one pair far apart and one pair close. Keeko's doubt: we can always tell by looking.
